findings.title: All integration chunks are started eagerly when appStore is imported
findings.body: Each `import("./...")` expression is evaluated while constructing `appStore`, so importing this module immediately starts loading every app package. This does not defer loading until a particular integration is selected; it can fetch/initialize all optional integration chunks on requests that only need one (or none), undermining the intended lazy-loading benefit and increasing startup/request resource use. Store import functions (for example `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke only the selected one.

findings.title: Recurring calendar deletions are no longer included in the awaited deletion set
findings.body: The async `forEach` callbacks are not awaited. Before this change each callback synchronously appended the calendar deletion promise to `apiDeletes`; now it first waits for `getCalendar`, so execution reaches `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 while `apiDeletes` is commonly still empty. The cancellation request can therefore finish and remove booking references before recurring external calendar events are deleted, and import/deletion failures become unhandled rejections. Build deletion promises with `map`/`Promise.all` (or await a `for...of` loop) before awaiting `apiDeletes`.

findings.title: Reschedule does not await calendar imports or external deletions
findings.body: `forEach(async ...)` discards every callback promise. As a result, this function sends the reschedule email and returns success without waiting for `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`; an import failure is also outside the surrounding `try/catch` and becomes an unhandled rejection. This can leave the prior calendar event undeleted while the booking is already marked cancelled. Replace the `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (and keep it inside the error handling).

findings.title: Request-reschedule returns before imported integrations are deleted
findings.body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is not collected or awaited. Since it now awaits `getCalendar` before calling `deleteEvent`, the mutation proceeds to send email/webhooks and resolves before deletion has even started; failures while importing an app are not propagated or handled. Await a mapped set of deletion promises (or use an awaited `for...of`) so the cancellation side effect is completed or handled before reporting the reschedule request.
